children: SYDNEY--New homes sales across Australia plummeted in October, stoking fears that a deepening slump in housing construction could slow the economy sharply.
New home sales fell 19.3% over the month, with falls recorded in all major states, the Housing Industry Association, which represents home builders, said Tuesday.
The drop in sales came ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia's announcement of a fifth interest rate rise in November.
Earlier Tuesday, RBA Governor Michele Bullock said that inflation risks remain skewed upward, highlighting the impact of oil prices and a boom in data center construction as key inflation risks.
Still, she also mentioned that the contraction in the housing sector could put a brake on the economy.
The fall in home sales comes as house prices are also tumbling across the country, prompting potential buyers to wait on the sidelines.

title: Australian New Home Sales Tumble in October, Industry Association Says
